transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dana (CTO, Orpheus), Rajan (Head of Security), Maya (ML), Oliver (Legal), Tess (Infra)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood team walked through security posture, encryption/KMS options, data residency, and data handling policies (prompt retention, PII/PHI handling). Customer asked for explicit confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data and for audit/logging details. Action items captured for delivering SOC2/ISO artifacts and KMS integration docs.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, RBAC/SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS/HSM, encryption at rest/in transit, data residency (EU/US), prompt retention, PII/PHI handling, no-training-on-customer-data confirmation, private deployment options (VPC, on-prem).

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Lena from Redwood, AE. With me are Marco and Samir from engineering. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana: Hi Lena, good thanks. We have Rajan, Maya, Oliver and Tess on the line as well. Appreciate you making time.
[00:15] Lena: Great. The agenda today is to run through our security posture and answer any questions about data handling, retention, encryption and assurances around not training on customer content. Marco will lead the deep parts.
[00:28] Marco: Hey all. I'll start with a quick overview of compliance. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II, we also have ISO 27001 certification for the control set we operate. I will caveat that the hosted API is separate from Dedicated/Private in terms of how keys and network are managed.
[00:43] Rajan: Quick clarifying Q: we need to know whether the hosted API ever uses customer prompts to improve model weights or training.
[00:50] Marco: Short answer: no. We don't train models on customer content. For hosted customers we persist prompts and responses only for telemetry and debugging according to retention policy, and they are not used for model training. We can provide the specific contract language.
[01:05] Oliver: Can you confirm that in writing? We need an explicit "no training on customer data" clause for our vendor security review.
[01:10] Lena: Yes, we'll send the standard vendor statement and the SOC2 exhibits that include that. We'll also share the security deck link.
[01:16] Maya: How long are prompts retained by default on the hosted API? We need to know retention windows for PII/PHI concerns.
[01:23] Marco: Default retention on hosted is 30 days for full payloads, but we have options: 0 days (ephemeral) for token-level logs, or longer for debug if enabled. For Dedicated or Private deployments, you control retention and logs remain in your environment if you choose VPC or on-prem.
[01:40] Tess: When you say "ephemeral", is that zero storage or just inaccessible? We need technical details for our compliance docs.
[01:47] Samir: Ephemeral means we don't persist conversational payloads beyond the request lifecycle for that option—only aggregated telemetry is kept. We can provide an architecture diagram showing the path and TTL.
[01:56] Rajan: Audit logs—what's captured? We need immutable logs for admin actions, role changes, API key creations, and who accessed what model/route.
[02:04] Marco: The audit log includes admin auth events, token issuance, role changes, and route-level invocations with request IDs and timestamps. Logs are exportable to your SIEM via S3 or a streaming integration. They are also tamper-evident—hash chains and retention policies are documented in the audit guide.
[02:22] Rajan: Good. SSO—do you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning? We want RBAC mapped to our IdP groups.
[02:29] Lena: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for Enterprise accounts. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. We'll share the SSO setup guide.
[02:38] Dana: KMS—we prefer customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. What's supported?
[02:43] Marco: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and for Private deployments HSM integrations are available. For Dedicated, you can bring your KMS keys with envelope encryption. We'll send a KMS integration doc and sample Terraform.
[02:59] Tess: Do you do envelope encryption and rotate keys?
[03:02] Samir: Yes, envelope encryption by default with platform-managed data keys; rotation is supported and we've got key-rotation procedures. If you use customer-managed keys, you control rotation.
[03:12] Maya: On the no-training point—are there different behaviors for fine-tuning/open feedback? If we run evaluations and share prompts, could that be pulled into any public training corpora?
[03:22] Marco: If you explicitly opt in to a data-sharing program for model improvements we would only do so with written consent and separate contracts. Otherwise there's no pipeline from customer data to model training.
[03:33] Oliver: For legal purposes, can you provide the endpoint for data deletion and how deletions are proven? We need proof of deletion for certain datasets containing PHI.
[03:41] Marco: We have a delete API and an admin delete workflow. When you request deletion, we return a deletion receipt (signed) that references stored object keys and timestamps. For Dedicated/Private deployments deletion happens inside your environment so it's under your control.
[03:56] Rajan: Data residency—do you have EU-only regions and guarantees that data won't leave region?
[04:02] Lena: Yes, Redwood Hosted supports region pinning (EU, US, APAC). We can provision EU-only tenancy to ensure logs and data are in-region; cross-region failover is optional and requires explicit configuration.
[04:12] Dana: What about developer/engineer access at Redwood to customer data for debugging? Is that strictly controlled?
[04:18] Marco: Access is role-based and gated by JIT approvals for support sessions. We maintain a support access log and require explicit justification and short-lived access tokens. Those sessions are logged in the audit trail.
[04:31] Tess: Are those sessions recorded?
[04:33] Samir: We log the request and the time window, and capture relevant request IDs. We don't record video of sessions. Any data accessed during a support session is logged and flagged.
[04:43] Maya: If we have PHI inside prompts accidentally, what's your suggested approach? We need a mitigation plan.
[04:49] Marco: Two things: use input redaction/PII removal at the client side before sending, and configure ephemeral retention or on-prem deployment. We can also run a small benchmark where you send a handful of sanitized prompts to test.
[05:02] Rajan: Pen tests—do you do third-party pen testing and frequency?
[05:06] Lena: Yes, annual third-party penetration tests and more frequent internal testing. We can provide the high-level findings and remediation timeline.
[05:14] Rajan: Are there any known critical CVEs in the last 12 months that impacted customer data?
[05:18] Marco: Not that affected customer data. We've had infra vulnerabilities patched; details are in the security report.
[05:25] Oliver: Liability and indemnity considerations—we'll review the standard contract language but will probably ask for specific addenda around PHI.
[05:32] Lena: Understood. We'll loop in legal and deliver the vendor security questionnaire answers.
[05:37] Maya: Performance question—if we do Dedicated in our VPC, how are KV caches and batch behavior handled versus hosted? Latency matters for our triage use cases.
[05:48] Marco: On Dedicated we give you control over cache size and placement; KV cache lives in the inference nodes and can be pinned per-customer. Batching is tunable, and we can set SLOs at the pool level. We'll share the Dedicated performance profile doc.
[06:02] Dana: Any surprises about data egress for analytics? We run downstream analytics on prompts and need to know what is shared with Redwood.
[06:09] Samir: By default we collect anonymous usage metrics and aggregated token counts. We do not export raw prompt content for analytics unless you enable that and it's under your control.
[06:20] Lena: Quick note, I'm dropping links in the chat to: security deck, SOC2 report redacted, ISO summary, and the KMS guide.
[06:28] [link posted] "https://redwood.example.com/security/deck-orpheus" (auto note: link placeholder)
[06:33] Rajan: Thanks. For the audit evidence, can we get sample logs showing a role change and the deletion receipt?
[06:39] Marco: Yes, we'll provide redacted examples.
[06:43] Oliver: On contractual confirmation: we'll need the explicit no-training clause in the SOW.
[06:47] Lena: We'll include that in the SOW template we send.
[06:50] Tess: On SSO: can we do SCIM group sync to map our "data-scientists" group to a specific Redwood role?
[06:56] Samir: Yep, SCIM supports group filtering. We'll share the attribute mapping doc and example payloads.
[07:02] Maya: One more small ask—can you share a non-prod endpoint or test tenancy so we can run a small regression with synthetic PHI-like data to validate redaction before production?
[07:12] Marco: Absolutely. We can provision a sandbox tenancy with ephemeral logs and a customer-managed KMS for tests. We'll need a quick scoping doc from you on desired throughput.
[07:21] Dana: That sounds good.
[07:23] Lena: Ok we're getting near the top of the hour—want to do a quick recap of next steps?
[07:28] Rajan: Please send SOC2/ISO artifacts and the no-training clause. Provide the KMS guide and sample Terraform. Share retention options and a deletion receipt example. Provision sandbox tenancy if possible.
[07:39] Lena: Yep, all that and we'll schedule the KMS follow-up with Tess for week of Aug 24. Marco, Samir will own the KMS material and sandbox.
[07:46] Marco: I'll prepare the KMS terraform + integration checklist.
[07:49] Samir: I'll produce the redacted audit log examples and deletion receipt samples.
[07:53] Lena: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the KMS follow-up.
[07:58] Dana: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:00] (call ends)

Recap (auto):
- Redwood confirmed SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture and no-training-on-customer-data policy unless explicitly opted-in.
- Retention options: default 30 days, ephemeral 0-day option for hosted or full control on Dedicated/Private.
- KMS/customer-managed keys supported across major cloud KMS; HSM available for private deployments.
- Audit logs and deletion receipts available; SCIM/SAML supported for SSO and RBAC.
- Action items and next steps list recorded above.

References/Artifacts shared: Security deck link (in chat), SOC2( redacted ) doc, ISO summary, KMS integration guide (will be sent), sample Terraform snippets (will be sent).
